summary.policy_note: Standard line 0.50 (default): set so about 5% of clean panels from separate calibration papers are flagged. Measured on simulated edits, not validated on whole real papers.

provenance.summary: Content Credentials read; manifest integrity checks passed. Signed by a certificate issued to Google LLC, not checked against a trust list here. The credential declares this image AI generated.

figures.label: uploaded image
figures.blot_note: No confidently identified Western blot panels. Other image types are not scored by the Western blot CNN.

checks.blot_resolution: panels from figures wider than 937 px are scored on a copy resized to a 750 px wide figure (training resolution)

synthid.note: SynthID testing is manual only. A negative result does not establish human origin. Our small experiment found whole Gemini blots detectable but isolated bands too small to assess.

limitations: Identical and near-duplicate whole images may be legitimately reused; read the source captions.
Whole-image matching does not detect copied patches within different figures.
The user-confirmed Western blot mode relaxes a heuristic gate; it does not validate modality classification.
No universal fake-image or AI-origin model is being run.
The CNN score is an uncalibrated anomaly index, not a percentage probability of manipulation.
Conservative screening uses a stricter unvalidated operating point and will miss more genuine edits.
Blot heat shows overlapping 32-pixel model patches, not localized proof or pixel-accurate boundaries.
Multiple flags in one figure may share a benign imaging or processing cause.
A copied-band candidate's matched location is not necessarily a separately detected band.
No finding is not evidence that an image is authentic.
The blot CNN was trained on ~750 px wide web figures; larger figures are screened on a resized copy, so edits made at full resolution may be harder to detect.
The same embedded PDF object drawn on several pages (for example a journal logo) is reported once, not as image reuse.
